en: I bow to the Mother Maithilī, who is eternal, stainless, pure, non-different from Rāma, the Great Sovereigness, the abode of all virtues, and the delight of Ramā.

Oṃ tat sat. Salutations to the Supreme Brahman in the form of Rāma. Now, once upon a time, while the Blessed Maithilī was seated upon a jeweled throne, seven sages—Lāṭyāyana, Kauñjāyana, Khāḍāyana, Bhalandana, Vilva, Ailākya, and Tālukṣya—spoke these words of praise to her: "Bhūr, bhuvar, svar! The earth with its seven continents; the three worlds; the intermediate space—all dwell within you. Āmoda, pramoda, vimoda, sammoda."
You sustain everyone; O Mother, bestower of the knowledge of Brahman upon Āñjaneya, we all bow down to you, we bow down to you.

Then Maithilī said to them: "My children, you are well, unharmed, and stainless; what is it that you desire which has brought you here? They replied: "O Mother, tell us all this: by those who desire liberation, what is to be recited, what is to be attained, what is to be meditated upon, and what is to be known?"

He said: "The two-syllable mantra *rāma* is to be recited; the three-syllable mantra *riṃ rāma* is to be recited; the three-syllable mantra *ruṃ rāma* is to be recited; the three-syllable mantra *reṃ rāma* is to be recited; the three-syllable mantra *raiṃ rāma* is to be recited; the three-syllable mantra *roṃ rāma* is to be recited. This indeed is the *tāraka*; this indeed is the release from bondage."

The measure of this "Om" is three and a half morae. Reciting these three syllables, one recites that [the Supreme]. There are indeed three kinds of suffering: the internal (ādhyātmika), the celestial (ādhidaivika), and the elemental (ādhibhautika). By reciting these three syllables, one destroys them. In the world beyond the realm of Viṣṇu, in Sāketa which proclaims auspiciousness, by reciting "Rāmacandra," who shines there, one is liberated from bondage; by reciting it, one is liberated from bondage. Thus ends the First Upaniṣad. 1.

Higher than the highest, the source of all qualities that are the opposite of everything to be abandoned, the primal cause of the universe, a mass of immeasurable splendor, worshipped even by the gods beginning with Brahmā—that Blessed Lord, the son of Daśaratha alone, is the goal to be attained; the son of Daśaratha alone is the goal to be attained. Thus ends the second Upaniṣad. 2.

He alone is to be known as the Blessed Lord, the seed-cause of the entire universe, he who is compassionate toward his devotees; he alone is to be known as the Blessed Lord. Thus ends the third Upaniṣad. 3.

They spoke to her once again: "Among all six mantras, which one is the most powerful? By chanting which one may we behold our own welfare? Tell us that, O Maheśvarī! She said to them: "All mantras indeed bestow happiness, bestow auspiciousness, bestow security, and bestow wealth. Even a single syllable uttered destroys the great sins accumulated over many lifetimes. Among those, moreover, the six-syllabled mantra (*ṣaḍakṣara*) is the most excellent; it bestows its fruit swiftly."

It fulfills every single desire. One who seeks liberation attains liberation; one who seeks heaven attains heaven; one who seeks a son obtains a son; one who seeks wealth obtains wealth; one who seeks knowledge obtains knowledge. Whatever one desires, one beholds it all as if standing right before oneself. Therefore, He alone is the most excellent; He alone is the cause of auspiciousness; He alone is to be recited. Thus ends the Fourth Upaniṣad. 4.

The Lord of Sāketa spoke this very mantra to Manu in the past, just as he spoke it to me: "To Hanumān, my beloved, most dear to me; to him who knows all, the Brahman; to Vasiṣṭha; to Parāśara; to Vyāsa; to Śuka. Such is this Upaniṣad; such is this knowledge of Brahman. Having bowed down, they said: "We have accomplished our purpose; we have known what is to be known; our desires are fulfilled; we are freed from doubt. You indeed, O Mother, are surely our Guru, our Guru. Thus ends the Fifth Upaniṣad. 5.
Thus ends the Maithilīmahopaniṣad contained within the fifth chapter of the Vālmīki-saṃhitā.
